title: Four ways to run it later
summary: `process.nextTick`, a promise callback, `setImmediate` and `setTimeout(fn, 0)` in the order they actually run, and which of them stops the server answering while it drains.

sources.author: Node.js
sources.title: Process: When to use queueMicrotask() vs. process.nextTick()

cards.front: Point to the nextTick queue on the phase diagram: timers, pending callbacks, poll, check, close. Which one is it?
cards.back: None of them: it is not a phase, so the loop never travels to it. It is drained to empty after every callback and between every phase.

cards.front: `process.nextTick` and a `.then` callback, both queued inside the same I/O callback. Which one runs first?
cards.back: The `nextTick`. Node drains the nextTick queue to empty, then the microtask queue, and alternates until both are empty.

cards.front: The same four lines log `sync tick promise timeout` as `.cjs` and something else as `.mjs`. What, and why?
cards.back: `sync promise tick timeout`. ESM evaluation is itself running inside the microtask drain, so a `nextTick` scheduled during it lands behind the promise callbacks.

cards.front: `setImmediate` and `setTimeout(fn, 0)` inside an I/O callback: which runs first, and why is that not true at the top level?
cards.back: `setImmediate`, because the loop is in the poll phase and check is the next phase it reaches. At the top level the loop has not started, so the order turns on startup time and Node documents it as non-deterministic.

cards.front: Which of the four has the most urgent name and the latest execution, and what does that buy you?
cards.back: `setImmediate`. It is the check phase, so it costs a whole turn of the loop, and that is the feature: reach for it to give the loop a turn, not to run something sooner.

cards.front: A 200-job queue recurses with `process.nextTick`. Each job takes about a millisecond, and the server answers nothing the whole time. What is starved?
cards.back: Everything else in the process: the nextTick queue drains to exhaustion before the loop continues, so no socket is read. `setImmediate(drainNext)` costs a turn of the loop per job and answers every request.

cards.front: Marking a slow parse `async` and awaiting it freed nothing. Which boundary did that `await` actually cross?
cards.back: A microtask boundary, not a turn of the loop, so no socket gets read in it. Yield deliberately with `setImmediate` between chunks, or move the work off the thread.

cards.front: New code needs a callback to run before the loop moves on. `process.nextTick` or `queueMicrotask`?
cards.back: `queueMicrotask`. `process.nextTick` has been Legacy since Node 22.7.0 and 20.18.0, and the docs recommend `queueMicrotask()` in its place.
